```{r}
#| label: setup
#| output: false
library(forestTIME)
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
```

In each inventory year, a plot is associated with multiple EVALIDs. 
We need to get this into a form such that each plot is associated with exactly one "EXPCURR" eval and one "EXPVOL" eval in each year in order to follow code to make population-level estimates of carbon and biomass.
Plots can change their association with these two useful eval types over time, and we have some questions about how to deal with this.

## Assembling data

```{r}
# Use RI as an example
db <- fia_load("DE", dir = here("fia"))
```


```{r}
POP_PLOT_STRATUM_ASSGN <- db$POP_PLOT_STRATUM_ASSGN |>
  fia_add_composite_ids() |>
  dplyr::select(plot_ID, INVYR, EVALID, ESTN_UNIT, STRATUMCD) |>
  dplyr::distinct()

POP_STRATUM <- db$POP_STRATUM |>
  dplyr::select(EVALID, ESTN_UNIT, STRATUMCD, P1POINTCNT) |>
  dplyr::distinct()

POP_ESTN_UNIT <- db$POP_ESTN_UNIT |>
  dplyr::select(EVALID, ESTN_UNIT, P1PNTCNT_EU, AREA_USED)

POP_EVAL <- db$POP_EVAL |>
  dplyr::select(EVALID, END_INVYR)
```



```{r}
pop_info <- POP_PLOT_STRATUM_ASSGN |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    POP_STRATUM,
    by = dplyr::join_by(EVALID, ESTN_UNIT, STRATUMCD)
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(POP_ESTN_UNIT, by = dplyr::join_by(EVALID, ESTN_UNIT)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(POP_EVAL, by = dplyr::join_by(EVALID)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    EVAL_TYP_CD = stringr::str_extract(EVALID, "(\\d{2})$", group = 1)
  )
```

## Example plot

This example plot has 4 inventory years.  In 2005 it belonged to 10 different EVALIDs, 4 ending in 01 ("EXPCURR"), one ending in 02 ("EXPVOL"), and the rest of other types.  In 2010 it **only belonged to EVALIDs ending in 00**, then in 2015 and 2022 it belonged to EVALIDs ending in 01, but **none ending in 02**.

Looking at the TREE and PLOT tables for this plot, it is more clear what happened.  In 2005, a set of trees was inventoried.  In 2010, the plot was not inventoried because of denied access and the trees were all recorded with STATUSCD 0 (removed from inventory).  In 2015 and 2022, a *new* set of 6 trees was measured.

```{r}
#| column: page-inset
pop_info_plot <- pop_info |>
  filter(plot_ID == "1_10_1_133") |>
  select(plot_ID, INVYR, EVALID, EVAL_TYP_CD, END_INVYR, everything())
pop_info_plot
```


Here's the same plot filtered to just include EVALIDs ending in 01 or 02, for ease of viewing:

```{r}
#| column: page-inset
pop_info_plot_filtered <- pop_info_plot |>
  group_by(plot_ID, INVYR) |>
  filter(EVAL_TYP_CD %in% c("01", "02"), .preserve = TRUE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  complete(INVYR = pop_info_plot$INVYR) |> #bring back 2010
  arrange(INVYR)
pop_info_plot_filtered
```

The first challenge: in each `INVYR`, choose at most one EVALID ending in 01 and one ending in 02.
We *think* that if EVALIDs have the same end year, the estimation units and stratum codes are guaranteed to be "compatible"  (i.e. the plot is not in a different stratum in the two evals).

We choose the earliest of the `END_INVYR`s shared by both eval types if both exist.

```{r}
#| column: page-inset
#| warning: false
pop_info_long <- pop_info_plot |>
  mutate(
    END_INVYR_01 = if_else(EVAL_TYP_CD == "01", END_INVYR, NA),
    END_INVYR_02 = if_else(EVAL_TYP_CD == "02", END_INVYR, NA)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    .by = c(plot_ID, INVYR),
    END_INVYR_min = if_else(
      any(!is.na(END_INVYR_01)) & any(!is.na(END_INVYR_02)),
      min(intersect(END_INVYR_01, END_INVYR_02), na.rm = TRUE),
      min(END_INVYR)
    )
  ) |>
  select(plot_ID, INVYR, EVALID, EVAL_TYP_CD, END_INVYR, everything()) |>
  filter(EVAL_TYP_CD %in% c("01", "02")) |>
  filter(END_INVYR == END_INVYR_min, .by = c(INVYR)) |>
  select(-END_INVYR_01, -END_INVYR_02, -END_INVYR_min) |>
  # complete(INVYR = pop_info_plot$INVYR) |>
  arrange(INVYR)
pop_info_long
```

::: callout-important
## Question 1

Is this correct to use the EVALIDs with the earliest *shared* end year?  Is it safe to assume that if they have the same end year they will be "compatible" (i.e. the plot will be in the same stratum and estimation unit)?
:::

Then, to make this "atmoic" (i.e. one row per plot x INVYR), we can pivot wider and keep only certain columns—e.g. we only need `P1POINTCNT`, `P1PNTCNT_EU`, and `AREA_USED` from the EXPCURR eval and because we've chosen the *same* end year for the two inventory types in each `INVYR`, the `ESTN_UNIT` and `STRATUMCD` *should* be identical.  I also add TRUE/FALSE columns indicating whether the plot belonged to an EXPCURR or EXPVOL eval type in that inventory year.


```{r}
#| column: page-inset
pop_info_wide <- pop_info_long |>
  mutate(
    eval_type = case_match(EVAL_TYP_CD, "01" ~ "EXPCURR", "02" ~ "EXPVOL")
  ) |>
  select(-EVAL_TYP_CD) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = eval_type,
    values_from = c(
      EVALID,
      ESTN_UNIT,
      STRATUMCD,
      P1POINTCNT,
      P1PNTCNT_EU,
      AREA_USED
    )
  ) |>
  complete(plot_ID = pop_info_plot$plot_ID, INVYR = pop_info_plot$INVYR) |>
  mutate(
    EXPCURR = !is.na(EVALID_EXPCURR),
    EXPVOL = !is.na(EVALID_EXPVOL)
  ) |>
  select(
    plot_ID,
    INVYR,
    EVALID_EXPCURR,
    EVALID_EXPVOL,
    END_INVYR,
    ESTN_UNIT = ESTN_UNIT_EXPCURR,
    STRATUMCD = STRATUMCD_EXPCURR,
    P1POINTCNT = P1POINTCNT_EXPCURR,
    P1PNTCNT_EU = P1PNTCNT_EU_EXPCURR,
    AREA_USED = AREA_USED_EXPCURR,
    EXPCURR,
    EXPVOL
  )
pop_info_wide
```

## Carrying EVALIDs forward

Now, the question is what to do about 2010 when we expand the data to include all years?  Should we carry forward the values from 2005 all the way to 2015 or should the plot *not* be used from 2010 to 2015?

::: callout-important
## Question 2

Which option should we use here?  Why would a plot *not* be used for area estimation in one inventory, but used again in the next, and how does that translate to our annualized data?

:::

```{r}
#| rows.print: 20
#| column: page-inset
#| tbl-cap: "Option 1: fill down between each inventory, populating only columns associated with eval types that the plots belonged to in those years."
pop_info_wide |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) replace_na(x, -999))) |>
  complete(INVYR = full_seq(INVYR, 1)) |>
  fill(everything()) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) na_if(x, -999)))
```


```{r}
#| rows.print: 20
#| column: page-inset
#| tbl-cap: "Option 2: Carry 2005 data for EXPCURR eval through to 2015, despite the plot not being associated with an EXPCURR eval in the 2010 inventory."
pop_info_wide |>
  mutate(across(ends_with("_EXPVOL"), \(x) replace_na(x, -999))) |>
  complete(INVYR = full_seq(INVYR, 1)) |>
  fill(everything()) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) na_if(x, -999)))
```

With the first option, the plot would not be used *at all* in carbon estimation in 2010--2014.
With the second option, the plot would be in the *denominator only* for carbon estimation from 2010--2022.

You can't carry the EXPVOL EVALIDs forward to plots that are only associated with EXPCURR evals because the estimation units and stratum codes possibly won't match (getting these to match is the whole point).  This makes me think that option 1 above is "correct".

::: callout-warning
Both of these options have an issue: the switch from one EVALID to the next **does not match the way we annualize data** in ways that may cause problems.  For example, in the annualized data, there are carbon estimates for the first set of trees for 2005--**2007** (the midpoint, rounded-down, between inventories).  Option 1 would include this plot in estimates for carbon in 2008 and 2009 which would cause an **incorrect underestimate of carbon** because of the "missing" trees in those years (switch to STATUSCD 0 at the midpoint means no diameter, no height, no biomass or carbon!).

Option 3: join `pop_info_wide` in before interpolation and treat all these new columns exactly the way we treat other categorical columns currently (i.e. switch them at the midpoint, rounded down) rather than carrying them forward all the way to the next inventory.
:::


```{r}
data_annualized <- fia_annualize(data_tidy = fia_tidy(db))
```


```{r}
data_annualized |> filter(plot_ID == "1_10_1_133") |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = YEAR, y = tree_ID, color = tree_ID)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
